beats: Hook: DeepSeek shrank its memory of past words to a few percent, and the model got better, not worse (line_mla_slim_shelf).
Recap: GQA shares the cloakroom racks between readers (line_kv_group_racks, pre-drawn for L03-02); MLA does something else: compression, not sharing (slides 15-16).
One small latent per token: the clerk vacuum-packs each guest's tag and parcel into one flat pouch, shared by K and V and by every head (line_mla_vacuum_pack).
The worry: unpacking every pouch for every new word would cost the savings back (slide 17) (line_mla_unpack_mess).

The trick: W_UK folds into W_Q, W_UV into W_O by associativity; the unpacking lens is ground into the reader's glasses once, like a loop invariant (her words) (line_mla_optician_glasses, line_mla_reading_pouches).
The killer: RoPE rotates each key by its own position, so no single pair of glasses fits every pouch (slide 18) (line_mla_turned_pouches, line_clockwork).
The fix: a decoupled RoPE key, a small separate tag (d_h/2) shared by all heads; content in the pouch, position on the tag (slide 19) (line_mla_luggage_tag).
Size: (d_c + d_h^R) = 4.5 d_h per layer per token = GQA with 2.25 groups (slide 20); worksheet: 14x / 28x / 56x smaller than MHA (L04 3-5) (line_mla_slim_shelf, line_balance).
Better perplexity, her guesses: like dropout (line_mla_hedge_trim), redundancy in MHA (line_mla_same_shirts), less interference between content and position (L04 3).
Pitfall: absorbed MLA adds compute on short contexts, so serving engines switch absorption off there (L04 6) (line_mla_one_sock). Takeaway.
Cover (line_cover_l03_03; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the clerk holds up one flat vacuum-packed pouch beside the bulky loose tags and parcels it replaced.

drawings.prompt: A long low table seen straight from the front. Standing on the table in one evenly spaced row are five identical round wooden display boards, each upright on a little foot and facing the viewer like a clock face without any marks. On each board one thin flat sealed plastic pouch (a soft vacuum-packed bag with crimped zig-zag sealed ends; NOT a tablet, NOT a phone, NO screen) is pinned through its middle with one round pin, and the pouches turn steadily like the hand of a clock, always clockwise and always further than the one before, never going back: the first (leftmost) pouch points straight up (12 o'clock), the second is tilted a quarter of the way over (about 22 degrees to the right), the third leans exactly diagonally (45 degrees), the fourth is three quarters of the way over (about 67 degrees), and the fifth (rightmost) lies flat, exactly horizontal (3 o'clock). At the left end stands the party guest (an invented young person: simple round face, dot eyes, short messy hair, a plain loose sweater, a large blank round name tag hanging on the chest), wearing large round glasses, tilting the head far over to one side to follow the turning pouches, puzzled. Landscape image 1536x1024; the scene fills about 90% of the width and about 60% of the height. The pouches and boards are blank. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.
